content.title: How to analyse the funnel
content.summary: Use uniqExact(user_id)/uniqExact(application_id) per stage, matched by application_id, order-agnostic. Do NOT use windowFunnel/sequenceMatch past document_uploaded — timestamps are not reliably ordered there and it silently undercounts.
content.body: Verified against atlys: destination_card_clicked->application_started is 100% ordered, application_started->document_uploaded is 95.5% ordered — windowFunnel/sequenceMatch is safe there. Past document_uploaded, ordering breaks down: document_uploaded->pay_now_clicked is only 50.3% ordered, pay_now_clicked->purchase_completed only 52.6% ordered (the rest have the later step's timestamp BEFORE the earlier step's). windowFunnel on doc_uploaded->pay_now_clicked->purchase_completed returns 1,264/20,446=6.2% reaching purchase; the true, order-agnostic application_id-matched rate is 7,054/20,446=34.5% (pay->purchase alone is 47.9%). Always join/match by application_id and count distinct, ignoring order, for anything touching pay_now_clicked or purchase_completed. Still cut by device, geo, and destination before concluding.

fields.windowfunnel_undercount_example: doc->pay->purchase windowFunnel level3 = 6.2% vs true order-agnostic 34.5%
fields.rule: windowFunnel/sequenceMatch OK for click->start->doc; use order-agnostic uniqExact-by-application_id for doc->pay->purchase

content.body: This section was originally minted with the `convention:` prefix, which this project reserves for genuinely general, cross-table rules (see convention:funnel_analysis, convention:segment_cuts). Its actual content was a specific lesson learned while building visa_status_sharing_events -- deduplicate by event_id/ingest_version before insert, because that table's AggregatingMergeTree MVs can't retract duplicates after the fact. A later review (express_checkout, see agent_meta.schema_proposals) surfaced this section via list_context_sections and applied its ledger/versioning/correction requirements wholesale to an unrelated checkout feature whose spec never asked for deduplication or corrections at all -- burning the full revision budget chasing a requirement that was never in scope. Real content now lives at dataquality:visa_status_sharing_dedup, correctly scoped to that one table.

content.title: abandonment_recovery_events — column-shift defect remains an active blocker
content.summary: CONFIRMED data-integrity bug remains unresolved: the landed table's values are shifted relative to declared column names, so reads and aggregate views over the landed data must not be treated as authoritative.
content.body: The executed proposal does not claim that the existing landed rows were repaired. Instead, it explicitly treats the landed table and aggregate state as untrusted, restricts production writes to validated staging, and requires a high-watermark cutover: isolate writes, record W, validate and deduplicate through W, build and backfill corrected targets, create live materialized views, replay post-W events through the same idempotent path, reconcile continuity, and atomically swap. Reminders without exactly one valid reminder_sent event are quarantined; reminder outcomes must retain the same reminder_id; valid sent events require a valid channel and nonnegative timing. The defect therefore remains confirmed with fix_status not_fixed.

content.title: Envelope data-quality quirks (not documented in base_context.md)
content.summary: duplicate_id ~3.0%, is_back_filled ~2.0%, os NULL only for android rows -- consistent across the original 8 funnel/supporting tables. The 1:1 user:row pattern and device_type/os taxonomy are scoped to those same 8; newer feature tables do NOT follow the 1:1 pattern (see entity:user).
content.body: The original 8 funnel/supporting-event tables (destination_card_clicked, application_started, document_uploaded, purchase_completed, search_typed, landing_page_scrolled, auth_completed, pay_now_clicked) share: duplicate_id ~3.0%, is_back_filled ~2.0%, os NULL only for android rows (~18% of android, never ios/web/Desktop), a consistent device_type/os two-tier taxonomy (device_type in {ios, android, web-user-b2c, Desktop}; os in {iOS, Android, Windows, 'Mac OS X', Linux, NULL}), and the synthetic-data 1:1 user:row pattern (one row per user_id) -- don't assume GROUP BY user_id collapses anything meaningful WITHIN THIS SET OF 8, it's already collapsed. Feature tables instrumented since (table:* sections not in the original 8) are NOT covered by this section's claims by default -- check each one's own table:* section for its real grain; several (e.g. abandonment_recovery_events) show genuine repeat events per user, the opposite of the 1:1 pattern. Separately: application_id-matched event pairs are NOT guaranteed to be timestamp-ordered from document_uploaded onward (confirmed by direct join, not sampling) -- treat any windowFunnel/sequenceMatch result touching pay_now_clicked or purchase_completed as suspect; see convention:funnel_analysis for the safe method.

content.title: visa_status_sharing_events dedup/ingestion note (table-specific)
content.summary: Raw sharing events must be deduplicated before insertion into the canonical table; aggregate materialized-view states cannot retract duplicates after ingestion.
content.body: The ingestion path should first deduplicate the raw landing stream by event_id, retaining the row with the greatest ingest_version and using payload_hash as a deterministic tie-breaker when needed, and only then insert into visa_status_sharing_events. Historical data must be deduplicated before creating or backfilling the materialized views. Empty event_id values should be rejected or quarantined. The executed proposal uses inferred internal AggregatingMergeTree targets so each supplied view is a standalone CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW statement. For production, explicitly managed target tables with separate TO views are preferred when the migration runner supports multi-step deployment. Destination should be validated upstream as NULL or a valid ISO-2 code. Retention remains a separate operational policy requiring documented TTL, tiering, or DROP PARTITION handling.

content.title: Daily abandonment recovery operational metrics
content.summary: Executed daily AggregatingMergeTree materialized view for operational event counts and daily distinct recovery/user states across recovery, timing, device, geography, destination, and channel dimensions.
content.body: The materialized view writes to atlys.abandonment_recovery_daily_metrics and aggregates by event_date, event_type, drop_step, channel, timing_bucket, device_type, geoip_country_code, and destination. It stores countState(), uniqExactState(recovery_id), and uniqExactState(user_id). Timing buckets are not_applicable for NULL elapsed time, invalid for negative values, followed by 0-2h, >2-12h, >12-36h, >36-60h, and >60h. The view is intended for operational event counts and daily distinct states; it must not be used as a cross-event attribution-rate calculation. Historical backfills require an explicit INSERT SELECT using the same normalized query after the raw rows are loaded.

content.title: Abandonment recovery episode metrics
content.summary: New executed episode-level AggregatingMergeTree target records one aggregate state per recovery episode for abandonment, reminder, engagement, resume, and reconversion flags plus abandonment-time dimensions.
content.body: The episode target is keyed by recovery_id and stores argMax states for drop_step, device_type, geoip_country_code, and destination, selecting values from abandonment_detected events by event-type priority, timestamp, and event_id. It stores max states for sent, opened, CTA-clicked, resumed, and reconverted flags. The supplied backfill and live materialized-view SELECTs are identical and filter to nonempty event_id, recovery_id, and user_id. Consumers must finalize the aggregate states when querying. The target must be created and backfilled before the live materialized view is created; it must not be interpreted as trustworthy until corrected, validated source rows are loaded through the remediation path.

content.title: Abandonment recovery reminder metrics
content.summary: New executed reminder-level AggregatingMergeTree target attributes reminder channel and timing and records reminder outcomes only when events share the same recovery_id and reminder_id.
content.body: The reminder target is keyed by (recovery_id, reminder_id) and stores argMax states for channel, timing_bucket, and hours_since_drop, with reminder_sent given event-type priority, plus max states for sent, opened, CTA-clicked, resumed, and reconverted. The backfill and live materialized-view SELECTs are identical and require nonempty event_id, recovery_id, user_id, and reminder_id. This target supports channel and timing rates with outcomes attributed to the same reminder identifier, but it depends on the proposal's validation rule requiring exactly one authoritative valid reminder_sent per recovery_id/reminder_id; invalid or ambiguous reminders must be quarantined. Aggregate states require finalization at query time.

content.title: Conversion rate
content.summary: purchase_completed users / application_started users (funnel-scoped definition, per base_context §4 note).
content.body: base_context §4 defines conversion twice, inconsistently: once as 'completed purchases / sessions' (headline number to leadership) and once, in a note, as 'purchase_completed users / application_started users' (the funnel drop-off dashboard definition). These are different denominators. Treat 'sessions' as ambiguous — no session table/column exists in the 8 raw tables (app_session_id is per-event, not a session-count entity). Use the application_started-denominator version; flag the sessions-based version as unimplementable as literally stated.

content.title: Drop-off rate (per funnel stage)
content.summary: 1 - (users at stage N+1 / users at stage N), distinct user_id, in timestamp order.
content.body: Computable directly against the 4 funnel tables. Measured whole-window step-through: click->start 15.4%, start->doc 13.2%, doc->pay 72.1%, pay->purchase 47.9%.

content.title: Forex Add-on Application Funnel
content.summary: Application-level aggregated funnel for forex offer exposure through purchase, with deterministic offer-time destination/currency attribution and purchased INR add-on value.
content.body: The materialized view groups events by application_id and records first nonempty user, destination, to_currency, and from_currency values using deterministic argMin logic. Destination and currencies prefer values from forex_offer_shown, then fall back to later nonblank events. Device type and geoip country use the earliest nonempty observed values. Funnel stages are represented as application-level presence flags for forex_offer_shown, currency_selected, amount_entered, forex_added_to_cart, and forex_purchased. purchased_addon_value_inr sums addon_value_inr only for purchase events. Queries must finalize AggregatingMergeTree states first, then regroup by the desired dimension; attach rate is sum(purchased) / nullIf(sum(offer_shown), 0).

content.title: Daily group application event metrics
content.summary: Incremental daily event and distinct-group aggregates by normalized destination, group size, device, OS, and GeoIP country.
content.body: `group_application_daily_metrics` is an incremental `AggregatingMergeTree` materialized view partitioned monthly by `event_date` and ordered by `(event_date, event, destination, group_size, device_type, os, geoip_country_code)`. It normalizes nullable dimensions to empty-string or zero sentinel values and stores aggregate states for all distinct groups, groups started, groups submitted, traveller add events, traveller remove events, and document-complete add events. Consumers must use the corresponding merge functions when querying aggregate states; incremental views require a separate backfill for rows that predate view creation.

content.title: Group application lifecycle summary
content.summary: One periodically refreshed row per group for lifecycle completion, add/remove churn, start attributes, submission timing, and submitted-traveller counts.
content.body: `group_application_summary` is a refreshable materialized view refreshed every 15 minutes into a `ReplacingMergeTree(last_event_ts)`, partitioned by `cityHash64(group_id) % 32` and ordered by `group_id`. It derives start/application/owner attributes from `group_started`, tracks first start and latest event timestamps, counts traveller additions and removals, flags add/remove churn, records submission status and latest submission timestamp, and retains the latest submitted-traveller count. Queries should account for refresh staleness and ReplacingMergeTree merge behavior when exact current-state results are required.

content.title: Current group traveller state
content.summary: Latest active or removed state per group and traveller index, including the latest explicit document-completion value.
content.body: `group_traveller_state` is a refreshable materialized view refreshed every 15 minutes into a `ReplacingMergeTree(last_event_ts)`, partitioned by stable group hash buckets and ordered by `(group_id, traveller_index)`. For each traveller add/remove stream, it selects the latest complete tuple `(event, docs_complete)` using `(timestamp, id)` ordering. `active` is true only when the latest event is `traveller_added`; a later remove or NULL document status is not skipped.

content.title: Executed coupon-code metrics
content.summary: Incremental aggregate view for non-empty coupon-code event volume, exact users and applications, applied discount cost, checkout value, and code-level segment performance.
content.body: Target table `promo_coupon_checkout_code_metrics` uses `AggregatingMergeTree`, monthly partitions, and orders by `(event_date, coupon_code, event_type, destination, device_type, os, geoip_country_code, currency)`. The materialized view includes only `coupon_entered`, `coupon_applied`, `coupon_rejected`, and `checkout_with_coupon` rows with non-null, non-empty coupon codes. It stores count, exact non-empty user/application states, discount totals for `coupon_applied`, and final checkout totals for `checkout_with_coupon`. Historical rows are populated through the explicit code-metrics backfill before the cutover boundary; live rows are then processed by the MV.

content.title: Executed daily promo coupon checkout metrics
content.summary: Incremental daily aggregate view for event counts, exact non-empty users and applications, discount cost, checkout value, and operational segment cuts.
content.body: Target table `promo_coupon_checkout_daily_metrics` uses `AggregatingMergeTree`, monthly partitions, and dimensions `(event_date, event_type, destination, device_type, os, geoip_country_code, currency)`. The materialized view `promo_coupon_checkout_daily_metrics_mv` writes `countState`, `uniqExactStateIf` for non-empty `user_id` and `application_id`, discount totals only for `coupon_applied`, and final checkout value only for `checkout_with_coupon`. The MV is incremental for new inserts; historical data requires the explicit pre-cutover direct target backfill.

content.title: Atlys — business overview
content.summary: Digital visa platform; north-star metric is pre-purchase funnel conversion across 120+ destinations.
content.body: Atlys lets travellers discover visa requirements, start an application, upload a passport, and pay. North star: conversion — visitor tapping a destination card to paid application, minimal drop-off. Funnel is seasonal (weekend dip, summer lifts leisure destinations) and mobile-heavy (iOS-first, large Android base, meaningful web cohort). Everything after payment (submission, embassy processing, issuance, refunds) is out of scope for this context layer — those systems aren't in the tables we have.

content.title: Abandonment recovery event history
content.summary: Executed canonical MergeTree schema plus recovery-episode and reminder-level aggregate targets; however, the landed base table remains unsafe for trusted production reads because the confirmed column-shift defect has not been remediated.
content.body: The executed proposal defines the append-only abandonment recovery event history with six lifecycle event types, millisecond UTC timestamps, a materialized event_date, monthly partitions, and recovery_id-first ordering: (recovery_id, event_date, timestamp, event_type, event_id). It preserves recovery, reminder, user, application, device, platform, geography, destination, funnel-step, channel, and elapsed-time attributes, with a materialized timing_bucket. The proposal also defines daily operational metrics, episode-level flags and abandonment-time dimensions, and reminder-level outcome attribution. These aggregate targets require explicit creation and backfill before their live materialized views. The proposal's rationale correctly retains the confirmed column-shift defect as a blocker: defaults are compatibility fallbacks rather than valid identifiers, and production writes should pass through validated staging with event_id deduplication, required-field validation, reminder consistency checks, and quarantine of invalid reminders. A high-watermark cutover and post-replay reconciliation are required before the corrected path is treated as authoritative.

content.title: Express checkout events
content.summary: Canonical express-checkout MergeTree table with an immutable landing and replay path, idempotent delivery handling, and checkout-specific eligibility, OTP, saved-payment-method, and payment-performance fields.
content.body:
Grain is one accepted canonical express-checkout delivery per row. The canonical table retains the shared event envelope (`id`, `delivery_id`, `payload_hash`, `timestamp`, `event`, client/device, geography, `user_id`, and `application_id`) plus `destination`, eligibility, displayed amount/currency, saved payment method type, OTP attempts/success, payment amount/currency, and payment latency. It uses `MergeTree`, monthly partitions via `toYYYYMM(timestamp)`, and ordering key `(application_id, user_id, timestamp, event, id)`, selected for the stated workload with a reported 2.62x improvement over the legacy baseline. No materialized view was created.

Deployment must also create `express_checkout_events_landing` as a separate raw MergeTree table containing `raw_payload`, delivery metadata, validation status/error, and nullable replay timing. Landing is partitioned by `toYYYYMM(received_at)`, ordered by `(delivery_id, received_at)`, and uses a configurable TTL covering the maximum replay, audit, and producer-contract remediation window. `express_checkout_replay_ledger` must track delivery status, payload hash, fencing claims, completion, and errors. Because MergeTree does not enforce uniqueness, replay workers use an external fenced compare-and-set lease keyed by `delivery_id`.

Canonical insertion is idempotent by `delivery_id` and `payload_hash`. A producer delivery ID is used directly when available; otherwise ingestion generates a deterministic nonempty fallback from source identity, source event ID, and canonicalized raw payload. Records without a stable identity are quarantined. If a delivery ID arrives with a different payload hash, both payloads remain auditable in landing, the delivery is marked conflicting, and neither representation is inserted into the canonical table until manual resolution. Replay acquires a fencing token, reads ledger state, validates the payload, checks for an existing canonical delivery, inserts only when absent, and completes the ledger transition with the same token. Crash reconciliation checks canonical delivery ID and payload hash before retrying.

Validation trims and uppercases geography and destination, accepts empty values as unknown, validates nonempty values as ISO-2 codes, validates event names and boolean fields, and treats event-specific co-presence rules as warnings or quarantine decisions. Amounts are `Int64` with producer-defined units; until scale or minor-unit semantics are confirmed, comparisons and aggregations must remain within the same currency, and populated amounts without a currency are quarantined. Accepted duplicate deliveries remain auditable in landing. Raw volume and OTP-attempt metrics count accepted canonical deliveries, while funnel, conversion, adoption, and confirmation metrics use distinct `application_id` or `user_id`.

content.title: Group application lifecycle events
content.summary: Executed canonical MergeTree table for group application lifecycle events, with validated payloads and three analytical materialized views for group, traveller, and daily metric state.
content.body: `group_application_events` is an append-only `MergeTree` table partitioned monthly by `toYYYYMM(event_date)` and ordered by `(group_id, event_date, timestamp, event, id)`. It supports `group_started`, `traveller_added`, `traveller_removed`, and `group_submitted` events. The schema includes millisecond UTC timestamps, a materialized event date, shared device and geography dimensions, application and group identifiers, destination, group size, traveller position, relationship, document completion, submitted-traveller count, and `ingest_version`. Check constraints enforce nonempty IDs, ISO-2 destination and country codes, valid group-start payloads, positive submitted-traveller counts, and traveller indexes for add/remove events. Canonical ingestion must deduplicate staged records by `id`, retaining the greatest `ingest_version`, before insertion; `MergeTree` does not enforce ID uniqueness. Late corrections should be quarantined after insertion. Three views were executed: `group_application_summary`, a 15-minute refreshable `ReplacingMergeTree` group-level lifecycle summary; `group_traveller_state`, a 15-minute refreshable current-state view keyed by `(group_id, traveller_index)` and preserving the latest complete `(event, docs_complete)` tuple; and `group_application_daily_metrics`, an incremental `AggregatingMergeTree` view for daily event and distinct-group metrics by event, destination, group size, device, OS, and geography. The summary and traveller-state views use stable hash-bucket partitions (`cityHash64(group_id) % 32`) to distribute replacement work. Historical data must be deduplicated before rollup or projection backfills. Monthly raw-table partitions provide retention, tiering, and backfill boundaries; TTL duration remains unspecified.
